dialogue.content: moved money between two of my own accounts for no clear reason.
checked the statement line by line for once.
said no to a group thing on cost grounds.
waited a few days for something and it dropped. bought it.
added something to a wishlist instead of buying it.
bought something at full price on impulse and returned it.
paid a small bill early because it was in front of me.
past about three weeks of watching something for a discount, it stops being a purchase I'm deciding on and turns into a thing I'm owed. by then I'm not choosing, I'm collecting.
that's genuinely how it feels by week four.
added up what the week actually cost. surprising.
looked up the price of the same thing in three places.
got a notification about a rate change and ignored it.
wrote down what I owe someone so I wouldn't forget.
bought lunch out twice and noticed both times.
cleared a tiny balance just to see it at zero.
checked the pension statement. understood about half.
everything I've regretted buying was something I'd been waiting on for weeks and finally caught in a sale. the things I decided on and bought the same day, I've kept and used.
found an old account with eleven pounds in it.
declined an upgrade offer over the phone.
worked out I've paid for something twice for two months.
